guideTitle: Best Pole Saws for Thick Branches (2026)
metaTitle: Best Pole Saws for Thick Branches (2026)
metaDescription: Pole saws with 10 to 12 inch bars and real torque for thick limbs, compared on engine or battery energy, bar capacity and staged-cut technique.
expertTake: The Makita XAU02ZB with a 10 inch bar and two 18V packs is the best battery saw for thick limbs, and the Husqvarna 525P4S is the best gas pick for repeated heavy work. The EIDOWA 48cc is the value choice for big engine torque. Any limb thicker than the bar, or hanging over a roof or wires, belongs to an arborist.
introParagraphs: Thick limbs expose the weak points of a pole saw: bar length, motor torque and the weight at the end of a long lever. A saw that prunes twigs happily can stall, bind or tire you out in a limb the width of your forearm.

Capacity is set by the bar, but whether the saw can use that bar depends on power, and manufacturers rarely state both honestly. The sections below separate marketing claims from the mechanics that decide how a saw behaves in dense wood.

products.name: Makita XAU02ZB 36V (18V x2) brushless 10 inch pole saw, tool only

specList.label: Motor
specList.value: Brushless, compared by maker to 30cc gas

specList.label: Cuts
specList.value: Up to 140 in 4x4 cedar on two 5.0Ah packs

products.description:
The Makita runs on two 18 volt LXT batteries in series for 36 volts, driving a 10 inch bar with a brushless motor that the maker compares to a 30cc gas pole saw. The shaft telescopes from 9 to 13 feet, and the maker quotes up to 140 cuts in 4x4 cedar on two 5.0Ah packs.

The tradeoff is that it is sold as a bare tool: batteries and a charger are not included, so the real cost depends on whether you already own LXT packs. Two 5.0Ah packs at 18 volts hold about 180 watt hours between them, which is why the cut count is high. Against the 8 inch cordless saws in this guide it adds two inches of bar and a motor tuned for torque, but it also adds weight at the tip.

In year three, the battery is the wear item, and Makita packs are easy to replace. Keep the chain oiled and the shaft collar clean, and work with the pole at the shortest length that reaches the cut. Thick limbs punish loose hardware, so check the bar nuts and the shaft coupler each time. Keep a spare chain, because a chain that hits dirt in bark loses its edge in a single limb.
products.bestFor: Owners of Makita LXT batteries who need a 10 inch bar without gas.
pros: Up to 140 cuts in 4x4 cedar claimed

products.badge: Best Gas for Repeated Heavy Work
products.name: Husqvarna 525P4S gas pole saw, 12 inch bar, up to 13 ft
products.description:
The 525P4S carries a 12 inch bar and a two-stroke engine built for regular use, with a starting system that cuts the pull effort. It reaches up to 13 feet and comes from a maker with a dealer service network.

The tradeoff is price and routine. A pro gas saw costs more than imports and demands mixed fuel, a clean air filter and a sharp chain. A 12 inch bar can cut limbs up to about 6 inches when you work in stages, and the engine keeps its power for as long as the tank lasts. Against the Makita it offers more bar and no battery limit, with noise and fumes as the price.

Stabilize fuel for winter, carry spare chain and check the shaft couplers before each use. In thick wood the chain brake and clutch see real load, so listen for a clutch that slips or a chain that stops easily and have a dealer look at it. Wear a helmet with a face screen, since falling debris is the biggest danger on thick cuts.
products.bestFor: Heavy pruning every season with dealer support.
pros: Runs as long as the tank

products.name: ECHO 25.4cc 12 inch gas telescoping pole pruner, in-line handle

specList.label: Handle
specList.value: In-line trimmer style, rubber rear grip

products.description:
The ECHO has a 25.4cc professional two-stroke engine, a 12 inch bar, a 20.6 ounce fuel tank and a telescoping in-line handle. It is a lighter machine than the 48cc imports.

The tradeoff is displacement: 25.4cc has less raw torque than 48cc, so you must let the chain work and cut thick limbs in stages. Engine quality helps, and a clean, sharp chain does more for thick wood than extra cc. Against the Husqvarna it is a similar pro-class tool with a different handle layout.

Use fresh mix, clean the filter and keep the chain razor sharp. With less torque than larger engines, the ECHO rewards a patient technique: let the chain speed stay high, cut in stages and avoid leaning on the saw. Its large tank means one fill covers most of a pruning afternoon.
products.bestFor: Thick limbs when weight at the pole tip is a worry.
cons: Needs staged cuts in dense wood

products.name: EIDOWA 48cc gas pole saw, 3.5HP, 11.8 inch bar, 16 ft reach
products.description:
The EIDOWA brings a 48cc two-stroke engine rated at 3.5 horsepower at 9,000 RPM, an 11.8 inch bar and a 7 to 9.5 foot shaft for a 16 foot working reach. It is aimed at larger seasonal cuts.

The tradeoff is weight and refinement: a 48cc engine on a long shaft is heavy and vibrates more than a pro saw. Torque is its advantage, since displacement gives headroom in dense wood. Against the ECHO it has nearly double the cc but less polish.

Check hardware after the first hour and use fresh fuel mix. A 48cc engine pulls hard through green oak, but it also makes more noise and vibration, so wear ear and hand protection and take breaks to protect your grip. Keep the bar well oiled, since a big engine heats a dry bar quickly.
products.bestFor: Thick limbs on large properties at a modest cost.

products.name: SEESII 8 inch cordless 2-in-1 pole saw, 2x4.0Ah, brushless
products.description:
The SEESII has an 8 inch bar, a brushless motor, two 4.0Ah batteries and a 6 to 10 foot pole, with a head that detaches to work as a mini chainsaw.

The tradeoff is capacity. An 8 inch bar handles limbs up to roughly 4 inches in a clean cut, so it is the entry point to this guide rather than its ceiling. The second battery lets you rest one while the other charges.

Check the head latch and oil the chain every session. Do not push it into limbs near the top of its capacity, because a small motor in a thick limb overheats the controller. Treat it as a tool for green limbs of modest size and pair it with a gas or larger saw for the big jobs.
products.bestFor: Limbs up to about 4 inches on a low budget.

products.name: YardenX 20V 2-in-1 pole saw, 8 inch, 15.5 ft reach, 2x4Ah
products.description:
The YardenX gives an 8 inch bar, 20 volt power, two 4Ah batteries and a telescopic pole listed at 15.5 feet of reach.

The tradeoff is torque: 20 volts in a thick limb will bog, so keep cuts to the lower end of the bar's capacity. The long pole also flexes, which makes aiming harder. It is a reach tool first.

Store the batteries indoors and check the pole locks. With only 20 volts, plan on a limb or two per battery when the wood is thick, and swap packs when the chain slows. A long pole also makes the head wander, so brace the shaft against your hip before starting the cut.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A clean cut needs the bar to extend beyond the limb, and a common rule is capacity of about half the bar length for a one-side cut. The Makita at 10 inches and the Husqvarna at 12 inches handle thicker limbs than the 8 inch SEESII and YardenX. Always check the maker's stated maximum.

A long bar on a weak motor stalls, and a stalled motor heats up quickly, so back off the moment the chain slows noticeably. The Makita's brushless motor is compared by its maker to a 30cc gas saw, while the EIDOWA offers 48cc. A 20 volt saw like the YardenX has the bar but less torque in dense wood.

Thick cuts drain packs fast. Cold weather and dull chains drain them faster still, so a sharp chain is the cheapest way to extend runtime. Two 5.0Ah 18V packs on the Makita hold about 180 watt hours, versus about 160 watt hours in the SEESII pair. A gas saw like the ECHO runs as long as the tank.

Heavier saws handle thick wood better but tire you quickly at full extension. Hold the saw at the length you will use before you buy, since a long pole multiplies every pound at the head. Brace the shaft against your hip or a stable surface when making deep cuts. The 48cc EIDOWA is the heaviest here, the ECHO 25.4cc the lightest gas saw. Rest often. Fatigue shows up as wandering aim and sloppy cuts, which is when kickback and pinching happen. Set the saw down between cuts if you can.

For thick limbs use the three-cut method: an undercut first, then a top cut further out, then the final cut at the collar. This stops bark tearing and pinching of the bar. On limbs thicker than three inches, cut the limb into shorter lengths from the tip inward, so each piece is light enough to fall safely.

If the limb is thicker than the bar, hangs over a roof or sits near power lines, stop and hire an arborist. Pole saws are the wrong tool for those jobs. Limbs under tension, split limbs and anything above a roofline carry risks no homeowner should take, and an arborist has the rigging to lower the wood safely.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered weight at the tip, shaft stiffness and reach. A saw that is too heavy to hold steady is a worse thick-limb tool than a lighter one with a sharp chain.

howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tank size and battery watt hours. Thick wood turns every minute into more energy, so runtime figures for twigs were discounted.

howToChoose.subheading: Gas vs Battery on Thick Wood

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: The Husqvarna, ECHO and EIDOWA run as long as the tank and have the torque for 6 inch work. They are louder and need fuel upkeep.

cards.label: Battery
cards.text: The Makita is the strongest battery saw here but still limits long sessions. The 8 inch cordless saws suit thinner limbs.

howToChoose.note: Gas for frequent thick work. Battery for occasional.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a 10 to 12 inch bar and long runtime. Storm limbs are often dry, hard and partly hung up, so work cautiously.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Husqvarna and Makita fit best. Leave hung-up or tensioned limbs to a professional.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you cut thick limbs every year. The Husqvarna and Makita justify it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if thick limbs are rare. The EIDOWA or SEESII is enough, and the money saved can go toward a professional for the one big limb a decade.

maintenance.why: Dull chains stall in thick wood and overheat the bar, so touch up the cutters with a round file every few tanks or packs.
A dry or loose chain damages the bar and can throw the chain, so top up oil at every refuel or recharge.
A slipping joint is unsafe at full extension.
Fuel, filter and spark plug, plus a check that the clutch cover and chain catcher are intact.
Cold shortens battery life and thick cuts drain packs quickly, so keep spares warm indoors until needed.

faq.q: How thick can a pole saw cut?
faq.a: About half the bar length for a clean one-side cut, so 5 to 6 inches on a 12 inch bar. Check the maker's maximum, and stage thicker cuts rather than forcing the saw.

faq.q: Gas or battery for thick limbs?
faq.a: Gas has more stamina. The Makita is the strongest battery option, but expect to swap packs on a big job.

faq.q: How do I cut a heavy limb?
faq.a: Use an undercut, a top cut further out and a final cut at the collar. That sequence relieves the weight before the last cut.

faq.q: Can I use a pole saw near lines?

faq.a: Yes. It gives more torque per battery, runs cooler and holds chain speed better as the pack drains.
Helmet, eye and hearing protection, and stay out of the drop zone. Falling limbs bounce, so plan an escape path before you start.
